summary:
Your volume has been remarkably stable — 127 km over the last four weeks against 125 km the prior block, essentially flat — but that consistency is sitting on top of a well-constructed recent sequence. The 44 km effort on June 8th anchored the block, and you've since managed back-to-back days on June 30th and July 2nd (11.7 and 13.8 km) at relaxed aerobic paces around 5:48–5:59 /km with HR in the 137–143 range. That's a meaningful durability signal: the paces are easy, the cardiac response is controlled, and you're accumulating it on consecutive days.

The standout session in the window is June 27th — 15.7 km at 4:49 /km with HR 161, load nearly 240. That's comfortably sub-threshold work at meaningful volume, and the pace sits well below your lactate threshold benchmark of 4:24 /km at 178 bpm established today. The gap between that threshold pace and your half-marathon PB pace of 4:18 /km is narrow enough to warrant attention — it suggests your aerobic ceiling is being pushed, and the threshold data will become more interpretable as daily values accumulate over the coming weeks.

Your daily step average of 14,120 over the last four weeks — including 11,641 on rest days — reflects a genuinely active baseline that doesn't appear in the run data. Combined with the bike commute, your total movement load is meaningfully higher than the tracked running volume alone suggests. This matters when reading the 20-week running streak at face value: you're not coasting between sessions.
